newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish gold prices mixed in steady volume.
newsitem.headline: Turkish gold prices mixed in steady volume.

text.p: Prices on the Istanbul Gold Exchange ended mixed on Tuesday as volume was little changed despite the latest tension in Iraq, dealers said.
Gold closed at $387.70 an ounce, down $0.30 from Monday in line with the European trends, and at 1,085,700 lira per gram, up 3,200 lira due to a weaker lira.
Traded volume was 1,162 kilos after yesterday's 1,150.
The lira eased to 86,980 against the dollar from Monday's 86,760 close due to a firmer dollar/mark parity in international markets.
"The market quietly awaited COMEX opening in the afternoon to see which way gold prices would go after U.S. missile attacks on Iraq," said a bank dealer.
Volume dived to 317 kilos in the second session from 845 in the morning. Some 54 percent of the daily total was in dollar terms.
Dealers said free market activity focused on currency trade rather than gold following the U.S. missile strikes on targets in southern Iraq.
"The peak of the seasonal activity in gold is over. We may see significant falls in daily volume in the second half of September," the banker added. --Istanbul newsroom +90-212-2750875
